title: Teach it three more rules
hints: Each rule is one more `case` inside the `match`: the pattern after `case`, and a `return` of the replacement under it.
Times one looks like the rule that is already there: `case Mul(x, Const(1)):` and then `return x`.
For two numbers, name both in the pattern and build a new `Const`: `case Add(Const(m), Const(n)):` and then `return Const(m + n)`. Do the same for `Mul`.

answer.explain: Each rule is one branch: a pattern for the shape, then the replacement. `x` matches any expression, so times one works on `(a + b) * 1` too. The folding branches match only when both children are numbers. `y + (2 * 0)` gets no rule, because its right child is a multiplication and not the number 0.
